_comment: Rookie seasons force-included into the Rookie set for players with no base card (the same role legends-2026.json plays for Super Season). Each entry names the rookie season explicitly, which is what lets Jordan's 1984-85 in past the archive window guard (1985 is the first cached season, so 'first appearance' cannot prove it is a rookie year — but it is). Picked 2026-09-06 under the capstone rule: a pairing with no card anywhere. The strongest by salary becomes the Rookie set's completion reward (set-rewards).

Michael Jordan.reason: ROY, 28.2 ppg; the user asked for it by name

Chris Webber.reason: ROY; BPM 4.0, VORP 3.6 — Golden State, no card there

Blake Griffin.reason: ROY, All-Star as a rookie; his only card is the Pistons reward

Vince Carter.reason: ROY in the lockout year; BPM 2.8

Hakeem Olajuwon.reason: 1984-85 rookie year — 82g, 2914min. The archive gap at 1978-1984 means a 1985 debut cannot be proven, so it is named.

Charles Barkley.reason: 1984-85 rookie year — 82g, 2347min. Same 1984-85 draft class as Jordan and Olajuwon; the archive cannot prove the debut.

John Stockton.reason: 1984-85 rookie year — 82g, 1490min. Same class; named for the same reason.

Karl Malone.reason: 1985-86 rookie year — 81g, 2475min. Sits at the loaded window edge, so the debut cannot be proven and is named.

Patrick Ewing.reason: 1985-86 rookie year — 50g, 1771min. Same window edge as Malone.

Gary Payton.reason: 1990-91 rookie year — 82g, 2244min. Forced because the archive lookup folds 'Gary Payton II' onto this name and returns the son's 2017 debut.
